sources.title: François Dumas, Noncommutative Invariants, Serie B: Trabajos de Matematica No. 60/2011
sources.locator: §1.3.1 iterated Ore extensions (PDF pp. 10–11); §2.1.1 Weyl algebras (PDF pp. 15–16 / printed pp. 11–12); §3.2.1 Heisenberg enveloping algebra and central quotient (PDF pp. 34–35 / printed pp. 29–30).
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 103-page university-hosted research monograph/lecture text by the author.

contents.name: §1.3.1: Ore extensions have a free coefficient-module normal form
contents.support: The notes identify iterated Ore normal forms for polynomial differential operators. The current theorem separately gives its complete local rewriting and characteristic-independent basis proof.

contents.name: §2.1.1: polynomial differential operators, Weyl generators, commutators, and ordered monomials
contents.support: Supports the polynomial Weyl presentation and the standard normal-order convention; the local theorem establishes the central-parameter quotient and proves independence in every characteristic. Its defining commutator is the F1 input to the locally proved finite-module trace obstruction; the source is not treated as proving that obstruction.

contents.name: §3.2.1: the Heisenberg enveloping algebra and its central-parameter quotient
contents.support: Provides an independent Heisenberg/Weyl quotient treatment. The local proof fixes the sign convention [P_i,X_j]=delta_ij Z and proves the scalar specialization directly.

read_evidence.access_method: Opened the author-hosted full PDF, inspected its extracted text at the cited sections, and checked the complete relevant paragraphs and formulas.
read_evidence.extent: Read §1.3.1's Ore normal-form construction, all of §2.1.1's Weyl definition and basis assertion, and §3.2.1's Heisenberg central-quotient example. The source's Ore-extension definition calls existence an elementary exercise; no omitted step is imported into the local normal-order proof. Its polynomial differential-operator realization is not used as a characteristic-p faithfulness argument.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Lectures on Calogero-Moser Systems, Lecture 8
sources.locator: Lecture 8, §§8.2–8.4, PDF pp. 48–50: Weyl(V) as a tensor-algebra quotient, Theorem 8.3 and its proof, and Theorem 8.5 (Koszul deformation principle).
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 74-page author-hosted lecture-notes PDF; the cited material is the full relevant lecture section.

contents.name: §8.2: Weyl(V) is the quotient of T(V) by the symplectic commutator relation
contents.support: Specializing the symplectic vector-space convention to the finite canonical basis gives the algebraic tensor-quotient convention used here.

contents.name: Theorem 8.3: PBW criterion for symplectic reflection algebras and its trivial-group Weyl specialization
contents.support: This is an independent comparison for the Weyl PBW statement. The current proof supplies its own Heisenberg quotient and diamond calculations and does not rely on the general theorem's Koszul-deformation proof.

contents.name: Theorem 8.5: Koszul deformation principle
contents.reason: The general deformation principle is cited without proof in these notes and is not needed for the elementary Heisenberg quotient; the local characteristic-independent rewriting and PBW argument supplies the present claim.

read_evidence.access_method: Opened the author-hosted complete PDF and inspected the full Lecture 8 text and proof passage at the cited pages.
read_evidence.extent: Read the Weyl(V) definition, the full statement of Theorem 8.3, Theorem 8.5's stated hypothesis/conclusion, and the complete §8.4 proof route. Etingof explicitly says Theorem 8.5 is not proved there; this batch does not import it as a missing premise. The source uses C, while the local item proves the Weyl basis over arbitrary fields.

read_evidence.access_method: Opened the author's complete textbook PDF and inspected Theorem 8.49, its double-sum proof, and the following operator-trace definition for scope comparison.
read_evidence.extent: Read the complete matrix identity proof in §8D. Axler's finite-dimensional trace argument is over a field; the local trace lemma independently states and proves the wider commutative-ring version required by the module obstruction.
